definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 defines class of a data item as 'A designation for a set of data items having common attributes or a common range of values', set by PICTURE/USAGE. 2023 says the same and moves the clause list into a note. The rule names categories in any case ('Use of the name of a data class or data category in the rules of COBOL refers to the category unless class is specifically indicated', §2002:8.5.2), so the governed items do not change.

cross-reference.answer: §2002:8.5.2 Table 3 lists the categories alphabetic, alphanumeric, alphanumeric-edited, numeric-edited, boolean, index, national, national-edited, numeric, object-reference, data-pointer and program-pointer. Each of the eleven 2002 category-name keywords names one of them, and index has no keyword in either edition. So ALL means exactly those eleven, which the pb415 cases and the init-cd probe show at --std 2002. Scope and evidence are unchanged.
